name: Wilmington
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Wilmington, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Wilmington, MA: Festival of Trees at Villanova Hall, Santa's Workshop, the Town Common tree lighting and the Santa Parade.
lede: Wilmington packs its first week of December with a Festival of Trees, a Town Common tree lighting, a Santa Parade around town and a Santa's Workshop for kids.
celebrates: Wilmington's volunteer celebration committee, the same group behind the town's Fourth of July and Fall Fest, runs the Holiday Tree Lighting on the Town Common with hayrides, cookies, carols and Santa. We're One Wilmington fills Villanova Hall with decorated trees for its Festival of Trees raffle. A volunteer crew drives the Santa Parade around town while collecting toys and food. The Recreation Department hosts Santa's Workshop, the library invites Santa for stories, and the Boston Metro Hi-Railers open their big model railroad to visitors.
lastyear: In 2025 Wilmington lit the Town Common on Saturday, December 6, from 4 to 7 pm, and Santa arrived at 5:45 to switch on the lights. The program had horse drawn hayrides, cookies baked by Shawsheen Tech culinary students, hot chocolate from the high school cheerleaders, glow sticks, an ice sculpture and carols from the a cappella group Soundscape. We're One Wilmington held its 15th Festival of Trees that weekend, and the Santa Parade rolled on December 7.
facts: Wilmington's celebration committee has been organizing town events since 1981 and runs three a year: the Fourth of July, which it calls the largest in Massachusetts, the Fall Festival and the Holiday Tree Lighting. The Festival of Trees turns 16 in 2026, so We're One Wilmington has raffled decorated trees since about 2011. The Recreation Department's Santa's Workshop goes back at least to 2016, when it was held at Town Hall.
trains: Wilmington has two MBTA Commuter Rail stops: Wilmington station on the Lowell Line and North Wilmington on the Haverhill Line, both with trains to North Station in Boston. Train fans also have a club in town. The Boston Metro Hi-Railers at 5 Waltham Street run a 40 by 60 foot O gauge layout with more than 1,500 feet of track and up to twelve trains at once, and hold open houses. Edaville in Carver runs a holiday train through the lights.

kidfact: At Wilmington's tree lighting, Santa himself switches on the lights on the Town Common, and kids get glow sticks to light up too.
faq: When is the Wilmington tree lighting?

Wilmington's Holiday Tree Lighting is held on the Town Common on a Saturday in early December, in the late afternoon. Santa arrives to switch on the lights, and the evening includes hayrides, cookies, hot chocolate and carols. The committee posts details on its website and Facebook page.
What is the Wilmington Festival of Trees?

We're One Wilmington's Festival of Trees fills Villanova Hall on Middlesex Avenue with decorated trees, wreaths and baskets that are raffled off. Admission is free, raffle tickets are sold, and Santa and Mrs. Claus visit during the weekend. It usually runs the first weekend of December.
Does Wilmington have a Santa Parade?

Yes. A volunteer group runs the Wilmington Santa Parade on a Sunday morning in early December, with Santa riding a route around town. The parade collects food for the Wilmington pantry, toys for Toys for Tots and letters to troops, and posts its route on its social pages.
How do you get to Wilmington by train?

Wilmington has two MBTA stops: Wilmington station on the Lowell Line and North Wilmington on the Haverhill Line. Both run to North Station in Boston, so families can ride in from the city or from towns like Woburn, Winchester, Reading and Andover.
